title: System.Data.dll is a mixed-mode CLR assembly, not a pure managed one
question: Is C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319\System.Data.dll a managed .NET assembly, and what does its PE and metadata actually declare?

environment: Static inspection only: REA did not load the assembly, resolve dependencies through a CLR, decompile C#, or execute target code.

commands.purpose: Classify the image and read its managed metadata statically

findings.statement: REA classified the image as managed with runtime family mixed-clr-native: the CLI header and metadata root are present, but COMIMAGE_FLAGS_ILONLY is clear, so managed and native analysis must stay composed rather than treating it as pure IL.
limitations: Static inspection did not load the assembly, resolve dependencies through a CLR, decompile C#, or execute target code.

findings.statement: The metadata stream set is complete and carries 14,072 method definitions, 1,140 type definitions, 9,096 fields and 17,650 parameters.
limitations: Static inspection did not load the assembly, resolve dependencies through a CLR, decompile C#, or execute target code.

findings.statement: The assembly declares public key token b77a5c561934e089, the strong-name token, and references nine assemblies including mscorlib, System and System.Xml.
limitations: Static inspection did not load the assembly, resolve dependencies through a CLR, decompile C#, or execute target code.

findings.statement: REA reported coverage state complete with no issues for this inspection, which bounds the static inventory rather than any runtime behaviour.
